Could NOT source the recorded owner 'Third Coast Midstream LLC' (100%) as the CURRENT owner — searched extensively and everything found points the other way. Current sources: the pipeline safety-awareness (PAL) mailer for 'BBT MIDLA, LLC' (pipelinesafetyinfo.com, Louisiana parishes Catahoula/Franklin/Concordia/Ouachita/etc. matching this line's operating area) and a Dec 29, 2025 PHMSA enforcement-response letter on Black Bear Transmission LLC entities (including 'BBT Midla, L.L.C.') stating those entities are 'now owned by Enstor Pipeline Holdings, LLC' (Houston, TX) as of the Dec 19, 2025 disclosure referenced in that letter. Public reporting (pgjonline, Yahoo Finance, gascompressionmagazine.com, Nov 2025) confirms Enstor Pipeline Holdings, LLC completed acquisition of Black Bear Transmission Opco, LLC from Basalt Infrastructure Partners in Nov 2025, and that Black Bear Transmission itself had earlier (2020) acquired a portfolio of natural gas transmission assets from a subsidiary of Third Coast Midstream LLC. That chain implies Third Coast Midstream stopped being the owner around 2020, and the recorded value is stale by roughly five to six years — current chain is Enstor Pipeline Holdings LLC -> Black Bear Transmission LLC -> BBT Midla, LLC (operating entity for this pipeline). Neither PHMSA doc nor the PAL mailer names 'Natchez' specifically (they describe the operator/company as a whole), so per the sweep's no-parent-trunk rule they are not offered here as refs for a value on this row -- they only support the contradiction narrative above, they do not confirm any owner value for this specific line. Flagging for Update/Status-review routing rather than proposing a value change myself.

verifications.note: Application under NGA Section 7(c) for a FERC Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity — the certificate class for interstate natural gas transmission pipelines.
'Midla: FERC-Regulated Interstate' — the operator's own current classification, matching recorded PipelineType=transmission.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded PipelineType=transmission confirmed: a FERC-certificated interstate natural gas pipeline under NGA Section 7(c) is by definition a transmission line, and the current operator's own fact sheet independently labels this system 'FERC-Regulated Interstate' (as distinct from the same page's several 'Non FERC-Regulated Intrastate' gathering/distribution systems).

Independent trade-press corroboration: 'The project is valued at $66.2 million.' Exact match, different outlet from the FERC filing.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded SegmentCost=66,200,000 USD confirmed exactly by two independent sources (the original FERC application and ENR's Feb 2016 trade-press item), both citing the pre-construction $66.2 million estimate. FLAGGING A DISCREPANCY: the completion-era press (Business Wire and Natural Gas Intelligence, both April 2017) instead describe 'the $60 million pipeline' / 'This $60 million project', and the $60 million figure also matches the face amount of the 3.77% senior secured notes that financed it (per the company's SEC 10-Q and 8-K). So there are two genuinely different dollar figures in the record for this project: $66.2M (the FERC-filed pre-construction cost estimate, which is what's recorded on the sheet) vs $60M (the reported as-built/financed project cost at completion, repeated independently by two outlets). Recorded value matches the estimate exactly, so sourced as REFS_ADDED, but the ~9% gap to the completion-era figure is material enough to flag for a validity look.
